memories.content: Do not exceed two primary HCI contributions.
Name each design or empirical contribution and present it in a single sentence.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the time burden associated with participation.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the travel burden associated with participation.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to identify primary contributions when named design or empirical contributions exceed two.
Emphasize the core design decisions that formative evaluation will change rather than a polished product demonstration.
Emphasize design principles transferable to other similar interactions as the primary contribution, rather than the performance of a specific prototype.
Formative evaluation creates grounds for modification in subsequent iterations rather than definitively determining the superiority of design alternatives.
List whom to notify and in what order if serious discomfort is reported during the study.
Field staff rely on the pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Define the thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies at which deployment and data collection must cease.
Establish procedures to restore existing systems and workflow states after suspending field deployment.
The user's stop plan can be judged feasible only when it identifies who has authority to order recovery and who is responsible for carrying it out.

In organizations where error reporting is linked to individual performance evaluations, safety signal records may be separated from research decision logs, potentially breaking the traceability path for the same incident.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational areas. The reference frame focuses on presenting HCI contributions, participant burdens, and formative-evaluation claims; the compared frame focuses on field-study escalation, stopping, recovery, and incident traceability. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: The reference frame alone provides both the contribution limit and its reviewer-centered rationale.
relations.summary: Primary HCI contributions should not exceed two because larger sets are difficult for reviewers to identify.

relations.reason: This presentation requirement appears only in the reference frame and is independent of the numerical limit.
relations.summary: Each design or empirical contribution should be named and stated in one sentence.

relations.reason: The reference frame splits one participation-burden requirement into its time and travel components; the compared frame has no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Community-participant studies should emphasize both the time and travel burdens of participation.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim governs how formative work is presented.
relations.summary: Formative work should emphasize design decisions subject to change rather than present a polished product demonstration.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim independently defines the preferred level of contribution.
relations.summary: Transferable design principles should be foregrounded over the performance of a particular prototype.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim limits the conclusions attributed to formative evaluation.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation supports subsequent modification rather than definitive claims that one design alternative is superior.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone states the escalation-sequence requirement and explains its operational use by field staff.
relations.summary: A predefined sequence should identify whom field staff notify, and in what order, when serious discomfort is reported.

relations.reason: This stop-threshold policy appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Explicit harm, disruption, and data-anomaly thresholds should determine when deployment and data collection cease.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim specifies the recovery procedure’s operational objective.
relations.summary: Procedures should restore existing systems and workflow states after field deployment is suspended.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim independently specifies authority and responsibility for recovery.
relations.summary: A feasible stop plan must identify both who can order recovery and who will execute it.

relations.reason: This conditional organizational risk appears only in the compared frame and has no scope-aligned counterpart.
relations.summary: Linking error reports to individual evaluations can separate safety records from research logs and break incident traceability.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance specifies discomfort escalation, deployment-stop thresholds, system recovery, recovery authority and responsibility, and a traceability risk created when safety records and research logs are separated.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance limits and formats HCI contributions, highlights community participants’ time and travel burdens, and frames formative evaluation around revisable design decisions, transferable principles, and appropriately limited conclusions.
